AP_visit_upcoming.description: An Authorised Person (AU home-education oversight) visit is coming up.

HEU_report_context.description: Background/context relevant to a QLD Home Education Unit annual report.

HEU_report_due.description: A QLD Home Education Unit annual report deadline is approaching.

HEU_report_literacy.description: Content relevant to the literacy section of a QLD HEU report.

HEU_report_literacy_section.description: The literacy section specifically of a QLD HEU report (near-duplicate of HEU_report_literacy — candidate for a future consolidation pass).

HEU_report_preparation.description: Actively compiling/preparing a QLD HEU annual report.

anti_corporal_punishment.description: The tradition's explicit rejection of physical punishment in teaching.

authority.description: The natural, loving authority of the adult the second-seven-year child needs (Waldorf).

badge_framing.description: Critique of extrinsic badge/reward framing undermining intrinsic motivation.

born_law_abiding.description: Mason's claim that children are innately disposed to accept just authority, not naturally lawless.

change_of_teeth.description: Steiner's threshold between the first and second seven-year periods.

child_argues.description: Child argues a point for its own sake or contests a rule as unfair.

child_asks_for_help.description: Child makes a specific, purposeful request for help or a resource (distinct from asking to be entertained).

child_asks_to_read.description: A young child asks to be taught to read before the tradition would introduce letters.

child_asks_why.description: Child repeatedly asks for the reasons behind a fact or rule.

child_estate.description: Mason's phrase for the child's innate constitution and capacities as a person.

child_resists_memory_work.description: Child groans at or refuses a chant, poem or table being memorised.

children_are_persons.description: Mason's first principle: children are born persons, not blank slates.

concentration.description: Montessori's central construct — deep, self-chosen focus that drives development.

control_of_error.description: Montessori's design principle: materials that let the child self-correct without adult intervention.

copywork.description: Mason's technique of copying a passage by hand for handwriting, spelling and literary exposure together.

deschooling.description: The general concept of the adjustment period after leaving conventional school.

deschooling_concept.description: Near-duplicate of `deschooling` — candidate for a future consolidation pass.

deschooling_progression.description: The staged, time-bound process of a family moving through deschooling.

deschooling_self.description: The parent's own deschooling — unlearning school-based expectations, distinct from the child's.

despise_not.description: One of Mason's three 'negative precepts' (paired with offend_not, hinder_not).

early_intellectualisation.description: Pressing abstract concepts and formal academics before the change of teeth (Waldorf warning).

emulation.description: Learning spurred by the wish to match a peer or model (Quintilian).

explosion_into_reading.description: Montessori's term for the sudden, rapid onset of fluent reading after preparation.

external_rewards.description: Canonical tag for extrinsic reward/motivation critique across traditions.

grammar_stage.description: Sayers' first trivium stage: collecting, naming, chanting, copying, retelling.

hinder_not.description: One of Mason's three 'negative precepts' (paired with despise_not, offend_not).

hoarding_dynamic.description: The pattern where past restriction (e.g. of screens or sweets) produces hoarding once access is granted.

holt_legacy.description: Reference to John Holt's foundational unschooling writing.

illich_legacy.description: Reference to Ivan Illich's institutional-critique writing (Deschooling Society).

imaginative_picture.description: The picture or story that carries a teaching before the abstract concept (Waldorf).

imitation.description: Learning by copying a model — Quintilian's imitatio (Classical) and the young child's imitation of adult deeds (Waldorf).

kitchen_table_learning.description: Mason's point that lessons don't require a dedicated schoolroom.

logic_stage.description: Sayers' second trivium stage: the appetite for argument, reasons and consistency (roughly 9–13).

masterly_inactivity.description: Mason's term for active, watchful parental restraint — not passivity.

material_conditions.description: The socioeconomic/practical conditions (time, money, a literacy-rich home) that an approach depends on.

memory_exercise.description: A specific memory-work technique or activity, distinct from `memory` as a broader curriculum area.

mind_as_organism.description: Mason's principle that the mind grows on ideas as the body grows on food, not a vessel to be filled.

movable_alphabet.description: Montessori's letter-tile material used to bridge phonetic writing before reading.

negative_precepts.description: Mason's don't-do counterparts to her positive educational laws (see despise_not/offend_not/hinder_not).

neill_legacy.description: Reference to A. S. Neill's foundational Summerhill/freedom-in-education writing.

normalisation.description: Montessori's term for a child settling into calm, focused, self-chosen work after real concentration.

offend_not.description: One of Mason's three 'negative precepts' (paired with despise_not, hinder_not).

onboarding_wizard.description: Surfaced during Hearth's pedagogy onboarding wizard rather than a Logger moment.

parent_availability.description: Whether an engaged adult is actually present for most of the child's waking day — the invisible infrastructure of home education.

performance.description: Presenting or performing an approach for an audience (e.g. social media) rather than living it authentically.

pestalozzi.description: Reference to Johann Pestalozzi as a forerunner cited in Mason's writing.

play_as_learning.description: The tradition's insistence that young children learn through play and that instruction should feel like play.

prepared_environment.description: Montessori's deliberately ordered, child-sized space that invites independent work.

radical_unschooling.description: The position that unschooling must extend to all of life, not just academics (cf. relaxed_unschooling).

readiness.description: Signs that a child has arrived at a developmental stage the tradition names.

real_experience.description: Mason's preference for firsthand encounters with real things over abstraction or worksheets.

reality_grounding.description: Montessori's preference for real objects and tasks over fantasy or pretend, especially under six.

recitation.description: Saying a memorised piece aloud, whole, to someone — the grammar stage's check and performance (Classical).

relaxed_unschooling.description: The position that accepts some parental decision-making (sleep, food, screens) alongside unschooled learning (cf. radical_unschooling).

resource_seeking.description: The child deliberately locating a resource or person to go further — the learner's half of the strewing exchange.

rhythm.description: Daily, weekly and seasonal rhythm as the organising principle of the young child's day (Waldorf).

sandra_dodd.description: Reference to Sandra Dodd's radical-unschooling writing and terminology.

science_of_relations.description: Mason's principle that education is chiefly the child forming relations with people, ideas and things.

self_government.description: Mason's term for children's capacity to govern themselves rather than merely obey.

senses_first.description: The senses as the root of knowledge; things before words (Comenius).

sensitive_periods.description: Montessori's windows of heightened receptivity to a particular skill or interest.

sequence.description: Ordering learning from easier to harder, whole to parts, without leaps (Comenius).

settings_reading_path.description: A parent configuring a reading-path setting in Hearth rather than a Logger moment.

silence.description: A deliberate practice of stillness (e.g. Montessori's 'silence game'; Mason's quiet), not merely absence of noise.

single_parent.description: Household context: one parent, or both parents working, carrying home education.

storytelling.description: Story as the carrier of teaching; told, not read or explained.

strewing.description: Sandra Dodd's term for leaving interesting materials in a child's path without directing them to it.

structured_freedom.description: Montessori's paradox: freedom operates within a deliberately prepared, ordered environment.

summerhill.description: Reference to A. S. Neill's Summerhill School and its founding premise.

telling_back.description: Mason's original name for narration — 'telling back' what was read or observed.

things_vs_words.description: Mason's 'things before words' — firsthand experience before verbal description.

thinking_love.description: Mason's phrase for parental attention that is both intellectually engaged and affectionate.

three_laws.description: Charlotte Mason's named 'three educational laws' principle.

trust_vs_neglect.description: The distinction between active, watchful trust and parental disengagement wearing the tradition's language.

university_transition.description: The late-teen move from home education toward university, TAFE, apprenticeship or work.

whole_life_trust.description: Radical unschooling's premise that trust in the child must extend beyond academics to all of life.

withdrawal.description: The parent's active, watchful stepping-back once a lesson or material is set in motion (masterly inactivity in practice).

work_cycle.description: Montessori's uninterrupted block of self-directed work.

writing_before_reading.description: Letters introduced out of drawing and writing, before reading (Waldorf).

wrong_work.description: Mason's term for work mismatched to the child's stage — the root of overpressure, not the child's fault.
